tema: Evaluates brain glial activation in fibromyalgia using multicentre PET.
diseno: PET with [11C]PBR28 (TSPO ligand) in 31 fibromyalgia patients and 27 controls from two centres (MGH and Karolinska), and PET with [11C]-L-deprenyl-D2 in 11 patients and 11 controls.
hallazgos: Patients showed widespread cortical elevations of [11C]PBR28 (VT and SUVR), especially in the medial and lateral walls of the frontal and parietal lobes, with no differences in the deprenyl signal. In exploratory analyses, fatigue was associated with higher SUVR in the mid-cingulate cortex.
conclusion: First in vivo evidence of glial activation in fibromyalgia, probably microglial rather than astrocytic; future studies should evaluate glial modulation as a therapeutic strategy.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on neuroinflammation, microglia and TSPO; the conclusions, taken from the discussion with a lot of funding noise, only provide the therapeutic implication. The study is in fibromyalgia, not ME/CFS.

tema: Evaluates the role of neuroinflammation and regional brain alterations in ME/CFS from neuroimaging studies.
diseno: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 65 observational studies (MRI, MRS, EEG and PET) with 1529 patients and 1715 controls.
hallazgos: Alterations were identified most often in the cerebral cortex, especially frontal, but the meta-analysis revealed significant hypoactivity in the insula and thalamus, nodes that connect reason and emotion with the limbic system.
conclusion: The findings suggest regional and neuroinflammatory abnormalities in the cortico-limbic network; larger cohorts and controls with other diseases are needed.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree on neuroinflammation, insula, thalamus and frontal cortex; the conclusions speak of robust evidence but acknowledge limitations, including inter-rater reliability.

tema: Examines whether long COVID, its CFS and its affective symptoms are associated with autoimmunity directed against neuronal proteins.
diseno: Case-control study: 90 long COVID patients and 90 controls; IgA/IgM/IgG against MBP, MOG, synapsin, tubulin, NFP, CP2, claudin-5 and S100B, HHV-6 and SARS-CoV-2; CRP and AOPP in a subgroup; regression and neural networks.
hallazgos: Multiple anti-neuronal autoantibodies were elevated; IgM-MBP and IgG-MBP were the best predictors of long COVID; IgG-MOG, CRP and AOPP explained 41.7% of the variance in CFS severity; the neural network predicted affective symptoms with r = 0.801.
conclusion: Autoimmunity directed at the brain, together with inflammatory and oxidative responses, contributes to the pathogenesis of long COVID and to the severity of its physio-affective phenome.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions (from a preprint version) present the work as a proof of concept, a more cautious nuance than the abstract's claim.

tema: Scoping review of MRI findings on the brainstem in ME/CFS.
diseno: Scoping review in MEDLINE; 11 studies met the eligibility criteria.
hallazgos: Structural changes in brainstem white and grey matter and functional connectivity abnormalities within it and with other regions are frequently described; mechanisms such as astrocytic dysfunction, hypoperfusion, altered nerve conduction and neuroinflammation are proposed.
conclusion: Brainstem deficits are associated with other brain changes and with clinical expression; the authors propose a model and call for better designs, larger samples and follow-up.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on the focus on the brainstem, white/grey matter and connectivity; the conclusions add the proposed model and the methodological recommendations.

tema: Compares the volumes of brainstem regions in ME/CFS, long COVID and healthy controls with ultra-high-field MRI.
diseno: Pilot study with 7 T T1 MRI in 10 patients with ME/CFS (CCC or ICC), 8 with long COVID and 10 healthy controls.
hallazgos: Larger volumes of the pons and whole brainstem in ME/CFS, and of the pons, superior cerebellar peduncle and whole brainstem in long COVID; no differences between the two diseases. Volumes correlated with pain and breathing difficulty.
conclusion: ME/CFS and long COVID show similar brainstem volume abnormalities that would contribute to neurological and cardiorespiratory symptoms.
triangulacion: Abstract and conclusions agree fully; the conclusions stress the pilot nature. Among the keywords appears passive optical networks, an erroneous term unrelated to the content.

tema: Proposes a theoretical histological strategy to identify the cellular unit that explains the pathophysiology of ME/CFS, pointing to neuroglia.
diseno: Theoretical review: compilation of 22 undisputed clinical and pathophysiological features and a literature search for explanations that point to a single functional unit.
hallazgos: CNS neuroglia (microglia and astroglia) would be the unit that best explains all the features, placing neuroinflammation as the central axis and integrating innate immune functions with autonomic, metabolic and stress regulation.
conclusion: Research should focus on neuroinflammation and the neuroglial compartment, with parallels in long COVID (PASC), where microglia could be primed by innate immune memory.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the discussion) are consistent; the conclusions extend the model to PASC, a focus not mentioned in the abstract.

tema: Compares the C-reactive protein response in ME/CFS with that previously observed in post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome (PTLDS).
diseno: Letter with case-control study: 131 ME/CFS patients (Fukuda and Canadian criteria) and 86 controls from the SolveCFS BioBank; ANCOVA adjusted for age, sex and BMI.
hallazgos: Recalls that in PTLDS CRP was elevated compared with controls with resolved Lyme (P < .001); the available fragment describes the sample and power (>95%) in ME/CFS, but does not show the results.
conclusion: Not stated in the available sources.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent on the CRP/PTLDS/ME/CFS focus, but the abstract is truncated before the results and the extracted conclusions are only funding and conflicts of interest.

tema: To investigate the relationship between CD24 expression, B lymphocyte maturation and energy metabolism in ME/CFS.
diseno: In vitro study with B lymphocytes isolated from patients and controls; stimulation with agonists, phospho-flow (pAMPK), proton NMR and MitoTracker. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Higher percentage of viable CD24+ B cells in patients after 5 days; negative relationship between CD24+ and mitochondrial mass (R2=0.76); correlation with glucose use and lactate secretion.
conclusion: CD24 expression is related to energy metabolism throughout differentiation and differs between B subpopulations.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions (with figure noise) confirm the link with AMPK in IgM+IgD+ memory B cells.

tema: Investigates whether a subgroup of patients with unexplained exercise intolerance has deficient systemic oxygen extraction as the main limitation.
diseno: Retrospective review of invasive CPETs (iCPET) from 313 consecutive patients with unexplained exercise intolerance; criteria for low systemic oxygen extraction (SOE) and hyperventilation.
hallazgos: Impaired SOE as the sole cause had a prevalence of 12.5% (32/257). The low-SOE and hyperventilator groups showed less acidaemic arterial blood owing to relative hypocapnia, and a low-SOE subgroup had elevated SvO2 at peak exercise.
conclusion: There is a cohort whose exercise intolerance is due solely to deficient systemic oxygen extraction, owing to muscle mitochondrial impairment, microcirculatory dysregulation or hyperventilation that shifts the oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve; it should be added to the differential diagnosis.
triangulacion: Keywords (hyperventilation, hypocapnia, mitochondria) and abstract are consistent with the conclusions. The study does not explicitly focus on ME/CFS; the conclusions add that hyperventilation should not be dismissed as psychosomatic.

tema: Identifies genetic risk factors for ME/CFS through combinatorial SNP analysis in UK Biobank.
diseno: Case-control study with GWAS and the PrecisionLife combinatorial platform in UK Biobank cohorts (1000 random permutation cycles), replicated in disjoint cohorts of CFS, post-viral fatigue syndrome and fibromyalgia.
hallazgos: 199 SNPs in 14 genes associated with 91% of cases were found, grouped into 15 communities of combinations of 3 to 5 SNPs. The genes relate to vulnerability to stress and infection, mitochondrial dysfunction, sleep disturbances and autoimmunity; 3 SNPs were replicated in post-viral fatigue and 2 in fibromyalgia.
conclusion: The study would provide the first detailed genetic clues on the mechanisms of ME/CFS and new avenues for diagnosis and treatment.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree (SNP, combinatorial analysis, UK Biobank, post-viral fatigue). The conclusions text (discussion) is a pathway enrichment table and preprint notices, with no conclusions; the abstract also points to similarities with multiple sclerosis and long COVID.

tema: Examines whether sleep disturbances, depression, age and intelligence modify the effects of CFS on memory.
diseno: Three experiments with CFS patients from a specialist clinic versus healthy controls: working memory tasks, semantic memory, psychomotor speed and the Doors and People test; measures of intelligence, insomnia and depression. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Patients reported frequent memory problems and a tendency toward poorer performance, but only speed and shape recall were significant. Depression, insomnia, age and intelligence did not modify the effects of CFS.
conclusion: Objective tests barely confirm the memory complaints; slowing could explain poorer immediate visual recall and the effects are small, so large samples are required.
triangulacion: Abstract and conclusions are consistent; the keywords (fibromyalgia, sleep) and the title point to another focus that does not match the content on memory, a possible metadata assignment error.

tema: Evaluates choice reaction time, encoding of new information, response organization and selective attention in CFS patients.
diseno: Case-control study with CFS patients (Oxford criteria) from a clinic and healthy controls; subjective measures and objective performance tests. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Subjective reports confirmed differences in symptoms, fatigue, mental health and cognitive difficulty; objectively there was only greater psychomotor slowing, with no differences in encoding, response organization or selective attention.
conclusion: Psychomotor slowing could be used as an indicator to evaluate the efficacy of different management approaches.
triangulacion: The abstract is opening text (introduction with background); the keywords are generic and the conclusions provide the results. There is a date discrepancy: metadata 2014 versus a 2022 publication in the text.

tema: Evaluates whether chronic multicanalicular vestibular canalithiasis (chronic BPPV) with a history of trauma can trigger the symptoms of vestibular migraine, ME/CFS and whiplash-associated disorders (WAD).
diseno: Retrospective, consecutive, observational cohort study at a private otoneurology centre; 163 patients with CVMCC and a history of trauma, subgrouped post hoc according to diagnostic criteria using a structured questionnaire.
hallazgos: 98% met Bárány Society criteria for probable vestibular migraine, 17% those of the ICHD, 63% the Fukuda criteria for ME/CFS and 100% of patients with WAD had CVMCC; repositioning manoeuvres improved pain and other symptoms in 90% of one group of patients.
conclusion: CVMCC can be the trigger of symptoms of vestibular migraine, ME/CFS and WAD, trauma appears relevant and the diagnosis received tends to follow the dominant symptom.
triangulacion: The sources are consistent; the conclusions are somewhat more cautious ('suggests' versus 'supports'). The keywords emphasize diagnostic criteria and trauma more than the vestibular mechanism.

tema: Editorial commentary on the study by Mandarano et al. on immunometabolic alterations in T lymphocytes in ME/CFS.
diseno: Commentary/editorial in JCI; no own sample stated.
hallazgos: Summarizes that CD4+ and CD8+ cells have reduced basal glycolysis, and that CD8+ cells show deficits in metabolic remodelling with activation and lower mitochondrial membrane potential.
conclusion: The paradigms of immunosenescence and exhaustion only partially explain the findings; unique immunometabolism mechanisms could underlie neuroimmune dysfunction.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions broaden the discussion on senescence, telomere length and disease duration. The brain fog keyword in the title is not developed in the sources.

tema: Examines whether cardiac dimensions and function are altered in women with ME/CFS, as a possible cause of abnormal lactate accumulation.
diseno: Case-control study with 16 women with ME/CFS and 10 healthy controls; supine transthoracic echocardiography with conventional Doppler, tissue Doppler and strain.
hallazgos: There were no significant differences in the key variables of cardiac dimensions and function between the groups.
conclusion: No echocardiographic differences were found in this cohort; studies during exercise and linking cardiac function to metabolic biomarkers would be of interest.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on a negative result; the conclusions add research proposals. The keywords focus on echocardiographic techniques and do not reflect the metabolic context of lactate.

tema: Describes the methodology of the two-day CPET to document exercise intolerance and the effects of PEM in ME/CFS.
diseno: Methodological article and review of previous studies with CPET in ME/CFS; provides no own sample.
hallazgos: ME/CFS patients do not reproduce CPET measures on a second test at 24 h despite maximal effort, because of the effect of PEM on energy production; the second test objectively documents that deterioration.
conclusion: The two-day CPET is useful for assessing functional capacity and exercise intolerance; the respiratory exchange ratio is the most reliable indicator of effort, preferable to predicted maximum heart rate.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the value of CPET and on the altered reproducibility. The conclusions add nuances (use of a single CPET for immunological studies and clinical trials) not present in the abstract.

tema: Characterizes cardiopulmonary, metabolic and perceptual responses to exercise in ME/CFS versus controls, with and without matching for aerobic fitness.
diseno: MCAM multicentre substudy with 403 participants (214 ME/CFS, 189 controls) in six clinics; ramp cycle ergometry to exhaustion; subgroup of 198 matched for age and peak VO2; linear mixed models.
hallazgos: 90% of tests reached criteria for maximal effort. In ME/CFS, ventilation, respiratory rate, heart rate and efficiency were lower, and perceived exertion (RPE) was higher; after matching for fitness, ventilatory inefficiency and increased RPE persisted.
conclusion: Compared with controls of equal fitness, ME/CFS is characterized by inefficient exercise ventilation and increased perceived exertion; separating the effects of deconditioning is key.
triangulacion: General coherence between sources. The keywords include chronotropic incompetence, but the PDF conclusions qualify that it was not observed in this large sample; they also propose exploring CPET-guided exercise prescription.

tema: Reviews the cardiovascular and haematological findings in ME/CFS and discusses the possible role of implicated viruses, drawing on what has been learned from long COVID.
diseno: Narrative literature review.
hallazgos: Atherosclerotic disease is not significantly associated with ME/CFS, but suboptimal cardiovascular function is (reduced cardiac output, altered cerebral flow, vascular dysregulation), not explained by deconditioning and perhaps of autonomic origin. There is evidence of platelet hyperactivity, abnormal coagulation, a procoagulant phenotype and endothelial dysfunction, and of herpesvirus reservoirs.
conclusion: Cardiac and haematological abnormalities are present in ME/CFS; it is important to determine their contribution to severity and whether they can be therapeutic targets, with viruses contributing directly or indirectly.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion are consistent (endothelium, coagulopathy, platelets); the discussion, with noise from a figure caption and declarations, details the viral mechanism of endothelial damage that is more speculative in the abstract.

tema: Describes the cardiological and clinical characteristics of Italian patients with suspected CFS referred to a cardiology service.
diseno: Observational study at the Department of Cardiology of the University Hospital of Pavia; 44 Caucasian patients with suspected CFS, with the diagnosis confirmed in 19 according to recent clinical guidelines.
hallazgos: Female predominance (ratio 4:1) and frequent history of infection with Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus and other herpesviruses. Most cardiological parameters did not differ between patients with and without CFS, but a significant association with low blood pressure was identified.
conclusion: Although it requires confirmation in a larger population, CFS patients show low blood pressure, which could explain symptoms such as fatigue, vertigo or difficulty concentrating and serve as a non-invasive biomarker.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion agree on hypotension and orthostatic intolerance; the discussion attributes the symptoms to autonomic dysfunction of central origin, whereas the abstract attributes them to hypotension, and stresses the need for confirmation.

tema: Presents preliminary data on catalytic antibodies that degrade myelin basic protein in ME/CFS and their possible role in demyelination.
diseno: Preliminary experimental study with patient plasma: isolation and characterization of specific antibodies that digest MBP and tests with inhibitors. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Some patients have catalytic autoantibodies that degrade MBP; glatiramer acetate inhibited this digestion and aprotinin (a serine protease inhibitor) prevented it, unlike other inhibitors.
conclusion: Proteolytic antibodies could contribute to demyelination and to symptoms such as neuropathic pain and weakness, and their study could open new therapeutic avenues, also after COVID-19.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent (MBP, demyelination, glatiramer); no conclusions are available, so the conclusion is derived from the abstract alone.

tema: Examines perceived stigma as a pathway between others' causal attributions and social and health outcomes in ME/CFS.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with 499 participants with self-diagnosed ME/CFS; mediation analysis.
hallazgos: Higher perceived attributions to controllable and unstable causes predicted worse satisfaction with social roles and worse functional status through greater perceived stigma.
conclusion: Seeing ME/CFS as controllable and unstable aggravates disease management and HRQoL; the study provides insights into the interaction between social perceptions and health outcomes.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent around causal attribution and stigma; the conclusions include noise about data availability that is ignored.

tema: Popular-science perspective on the cell danger response (CDR), which connects environmental health with mitochondria and the rise in chronic diseases.
diseno: Theoretical perspective article; no population or empirical methods.
hallazgos: The CDR is a universal response to threats that regulate mitochondria; it describes the burden of more than 7,000 chemicals and 83 billion pounds of plastic waste per year, and the rise in chronic diseases (40% of children, 90% of adults over 65 in 2018).
conclusion: Proposes using metabolomics and exposomics to correlate chemical exposures with disease patterns and prioritize molecules for legislative action.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent on environmental health and mitochondria; the extracted conclusions are acknowledgements and funding, and ME/CFS appears only tangentially in them.

tema: Investigates cellular immune function and herpesvirus serostatus in a large ME/CFS cohort from the UK biobank.
diseno: Case-control study: 251 patients (54 severe), 107 healthy controls and 46 with multiple sclerosis; serology of six herpesviruses and T, B, NK and monocyte populations by cytometry.
hallazgos: There were no differences in herpesvirus seroprevalence or in the number, subtypes or in vitro response of NK cells; effector memory and intermediate CD8+ T cells were reduced and MAIT cells increased, especially in severe cases.
conclusion: There is an altered immunological state, especially in severe patients, that could reflect recent infection or greater susceptibility; longitudinal studies are needed.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent (MAIT cells, T subpopulations, NK); the extracted conclusions are only contributions and funding. Notably, the abstract contradicts previous findings on NK cells.

tema: To investigate cellular bioenergetic abnormalities in PBMC of CFS patients.
diseno: Preliminary case-control study with PBMC from patients and controls; OXPHOS and glycolysis assays (XFe96). Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: OXPHOS parameters consistently lower in patients; maximal respiration was the key parameter (p≤0.003).
conclusion: CFS PBMC fail to meet energy demand, although whether this is cause or consequence is not established; they could serve as a therapeutic model.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions (with contribution noise) are more cautious in clarifying that cause cannot be distinguished from consequence.

tema: Evaluates in murine models the hypothesis that central serotonergic hyperactivity induces a pathophysiology similar to ME/CFS.
diseno: Experimental study in mice: high-dose SSRI, 5-HT synthesis inhibitor and viral vector to silence Htr1a; fatigue tests (rota-rod, wheel, cage activity), associated symptoms and HPA axis response to exercise.
hallazgos: Excess serotonin in the dorsal raphe nucleus caused intense fatigue, symptoms associated with ME/CFS and HPA axis dysfunction in response to exercise, effects verified with the synthesis inhibitor and 5-HT1A silencing.
conclusion: 5-HTergic hyperactivity would be implicated in the pathophysiology of ME/CFS and the animal model would be useful for studying the disease and its treatments.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; the extracted conclusions are acknowledgements and declarations, although they include a caption that mentions 5-HT1A receptor desensitization and involvement of the HPA axis and the autonomic nervous system.
